entries.decision_rule: Written before any run. Same UNIFORM recipe as trend8 (plain RGB, --no-hillshade, policy-C criterion) so every overlap delta is an instrument term, never a recipe term. READS: (a) |fraction(2017 CoE) - fraction(2017 King)| is the same-window cross-delivery floor at May; if it exceeds the 1.3pp same-flight bound (C3) the noise model is understated - STOP and re-derive before quoting any map number again. (b) The 2017 quartet decomposes: season main effect = mean(Aug arms) - mean(May arms); grid main effect within season; interaction. If season+grid explain <50% of the quartet spread, a fourth mechanism is at work (mosaic seams, BRDF) and the harmonization program is declared BOUNDED. (c) EagleView 2020->2022->2024 net change, method-controlled: primary read is SIGN vs Panel A on the shared window; agreement rehabilitates method-controlled map differencing, disagreement kills map differencing here even under total method control (either way a finding, pre-registered). trend8_2024 is reused as the 2024 arm - same recipe, no rerun. 2xA100 cap; approved by Kam 2026-09-05 ("Yes to 1 through 8").

entries.hypothesis: Items 2+5+7 of the flicker-program ranking (2026-09-05, Kam-approved): the archive's OVERLAP structure can decompose the trend8 sawtooth into instrument mechanisms without any new ground truth. (2) OVERLAP FLOOR: same-window acquisitions delivered differently bound the instrument term - 2017 CoE vs 2017 King share the May 4-10 2017 flight window (fine vs ~15cm grid); zero real change between them by construction. (5) EAGLEVIEW TRIPLE: 2020/2022/2024 CoE 5cm - vendor, GSD, and season all held; the strongest same-method series the archive owns; its 2020->2024 net is the method-controlled map trend to sign-test against Panel A (-2.21pp). (7) SEASON x GRID FACTORIAL 2017: {May: CoE 5cm, King 15cm} x {Aug: 2017s 30cm, 2017n 1m} - the only design that crosses season and grid with zero real change inside one calendar year.

entries.name: overlap_floor
entries.verdict: All three pre-registered reads complete, at policy-C matched cuts (the rule as written; delivered-cut fractions were never valid inputs). (a) FLOOR: |2017 CoE - 2017 King| same-window = 0.15pp - PASS at one-ninth of the 1.3pp same-flight bound; noise model holds. (b) FACTORIAL: quartet spread 10.1pp (delivered) -> 3.55pp (matched); the three <=30cm arms agree to 0.15pp TOTAL; season effect ~0 within grid class; the ENTIRE residual is the 1m NAIP arm (-3.5pp genuine information deficit, recall .73 at common precision). Decomposition: 10.1 = ~6.5 operating point + ~3.5 coarse- grid info loss + ~0 season + ~0.15 delivery-at-<=30cm. Harmonization program NOT bounded - the spread is explained. (c) EAGLEVIEW: 24.44 -> 26.32 -> 23.50; endpoints -0.94pp/4yr agree with Panel A in sign AND pace (~-1.1 expected); interior +1.9/-2.8 wobble - single-year steps stay inside noise even under total method control. Levels harmonized-to-C-CAP. Data: overlap_factorial_read.csv, eagleview_sign_test.csv.

entries.decision_rule: Written before any run. UNIFORM RECIPE IS THE POINT: all 8 arms plain RGB (--no-hillshade, 3-band; 2016 trains on its RGB bands only via the uniform flag set), same architecture, same policy-C threshold criterion (f1_plateau_hi_d005 vs ccap_2021_hires_lc, citywide dense sweep) applied identically to every year - C-CAP is the operating-point selector ONLY, never the accuracy or trend authority (it is a bounded comparator; Kam 2026-09-03). TREND READ: canopy fraction per year = postproc mask area / city area on the analysis grid; pre-vs-post-2016 slopes compared with the C3 processing-noise term (+-1.3pp single-year) carried as the error floor; the map series CORROBORATES the human-measured direction, it never overrides Panel A. Sign agreement map-vs-PanelA on 2016->2024 is the primary triangulation. Hot spots: loss patches present in >=2 consecutive maps, cross- referenced against Panel A verified losses + lidar loss cells. Per-session runtime limit (~7.5h) is expected to kill runtimes mid-queue: resume via explicit --only missing-list relaunch (the resume-credit hole is a known open debt). 2xA100 cap; Kam approved GPU + credits 2026-09-04.
entries.headline: DELIVERED-CUT SERIES RETRACTED as a trend read (per-arm best-F1 cuts on 650x-skewed eval populations; the 2026-09-06 attack).
entries.hypothesis: The canopy trend has an inflection near 2016: up-or-flat before, declining after (Panel A human measurement: -2.21pp 2016->2024, CI [-3.31,-1.11]; lidar physics: net gain 2005->2016 on covered ground). An 8-year full-city map series under ONE DELIBERATELY UNIFORM recipe (plain RGB, no NIR, no lidar input, no hillshade - per-year-best recipes change the METHOD over time, and a method change at the inflection year is a fake-trend generator) tests: (a) does the map-differenced 2016->2024 net agree in SIGN with Panel A; (b) is the pre-2016 slope (2009/2011s/2013/2015) >= the post-2016 slope (2016/2019/2021/2024), computed WITHIN the King sensor family where possible; (c) do loss hot-spots persist across consecutive years (a real hot spot repeats; an artifact flickers - the C3 same-flight floor 1.3pp/IoU .738 and flicker report are the judges); (d) do map losses co-locate with the 42 Panel-A-verified loss points and the dual-epoch lidar loss cells.
entries.metric: canopy fraction per year (postproc mask area / city area, analysis grid); primary triangulation = SIGN of map-differenced 2016->2024 net vs Panel A -2.21pp; secondary = pre-vs-post-2016 slope difference against the +-1.3pp C3 processing floor.
entries.name: trend8_uniform_rgb
entries.verdict: DELIVERED-CUT SERIES RETRACTED as a trend read (per-arm best-F1 cuts on 650x-skewed eval populations; the 2026-09-06 attack). At policy-C matched cuts (joint plateau, common precision .7394): (a) SIGN TEST vs Panel A: PASSES - 2016->2024 = -5.59pp sweep-footprint / -3.48pp city-clipped masks (delivered cuts had said +4.2, wrong sign); (b) pre-2016 flat-to-up, post-2016 declining - the two-leg story reproduced; (c) hot spots dispersed (largest recut persistent cluster 1.53ha); (d) 41/42 of Panel A verified losses corroborated by matched-cut map loss (was 34/42). RESIDUALS: +-2-4pp inter-year jitter persists (per-year curve shape) - single-year map steps are NOT readable; pixel flicker did NOT collapse (47.8% vs 50.7% of ever-canopy) - per-pixel instability is real detection noise, so change MAPS need persistence filtering even though change TOTALS at matched cuts corroborate direction. Levels are harmonized-to-C-CAP (matcher, never authority); pace authority remains Panel A -2.21+-1.10. Data: trend8_policy_cuts.csv, trend8_harmonized_fractions.csv, trend8_transition_census.csv, trend8_hotspot_map.png, eagleview_sign_test.csv.

entries.decision_rule: RECONSTRUCTED (retrospective: true) from the instrument docstring and the power gate that ran BEFORE the labelling — those parts genuinely are pre-registered. qc/instruments/paired_change_power.py was run first and gated the design: N=250 FAILED, N=1250 was GO at power 0.81 with a half-width of 1.03pp; the campaign did not proceed at the failing N. Pairing is the design commitment — one interpreter, the same physical point in both epochs, locators that LOCATE and never label. The estimate is admissible only if the controls hold: the SRS capture stratum bounds what the locators missed, blind duplicates bound differential interpreter error, a blur control bounds sharpness asymmetry between a 1-ft and a 3-in product, and a worst-case registration shift bounds displacement. entries.headline: DIRECTION IS DOWN, and it is the project's only human-measured trend statement.
entries.hypothesis: The city's question is DIRECTION, and no instrument in the pipeline could answer it: every map-based read of 2016->2024 was inside its own processing noise. A HUMAN judging the same physical point in both years, side by side, cancels the model, the threshold, the reference vintage, the radiometry and the interpreter's private canopy definition — everything the map series cannot hold still. What would change our mind: a capture audit finding substantial change outside the locators (the strata would then be measuring the locators, not the city), or a duplicate/blur control showing the interpreter manufactures change at a rate comparable to the effect.

entries.verdict: DIRECTION IS DOWN, and it is the project's only human-measured trend statement. Net 2016->2024 = -2.21pp of city area, 95% CI [-3.31, -1.11] — the single figure the city statement rests on, read from phase4/qc/panel_a_estimate.txt, which also carries every control in the same file. All four controls hold: the SRS capture audit found change outside the locators at a rate consistent with capture ~0.9+, blind duplicates disagreed at a rate the file records against its own gate, the blur control produced zero false change in 30 pairs, and a hostile 2.0 m registration shift moves the net in the direction that SUBTRACTS from the decline, so the sign holds in both scenarios. Loss points survive scrutiny far better than gain points (crosscheck in phase4/qc/panel_a_loss_crosscheck.csv). Kam's own catch during the verify pass is part of the record: the 2024 flight is leaf-off March-May, so a leaf-on October-2023 comparison was re-called rather than trusted (phase4/qc/panel_a_verify.csv). STANDING: Panel A is the PACE AND DIRECTION AUTHORITY. Map series corroborate it and never override it — that hierarchy is what trend8_uniform_rgb's retraction enforced, and what overlap_floor's EagleView sign test independently agreed with.

entries.decision_rule: RECONSTRUCTED (retrospective: true) from the instrument docstring, which states the reading rule before any number: the pair carries ZERO engine diff between the two pilot arms' commits, so mask disagreement between them is processing-chain plus GSD and nothing else. The 1-px-tolerant variant is what splits boundary jitter from body-level disagreement — the tolerant number is the honest floor for AREA claims, the raw number for per-pixel claims. Any later single-year map step smaller than this floor is UNREADABLE, not "no change" (CLAUDE.md 3.5).

See entry same_flight_pair_2019.

entries.headline: THE FLOOR EXISTS AND IT IS LARGE ENOUGH TO MATTER.
entries.hypothesis: Every accuracy number in this project is scored against a reference that is itself imperfect, so no reference can tell us how much of a year-to-year map difference is processing rather than trees. One pair in the archive can: 2019s and 2019n are ONE Hexagon flight delivered two ways (WA consortium 1 ft, USDA NAIP 60 cm). Identical sun, atmosphere, phenology and sensor hardware; only the delivered GSD and the processing chain differ. Whatever those two masks disagree about is a floor — no accuracy or trend claim about either product can honestly be tighter than it.
entries.metric: phase4/qc/sameflight_consistency.csv — one row: overall disagreement fraction, canopy IoU, and a 1-px-tolerant disagreement fraction over the valid overlap, after warping the 2019n mask (nearest) onto the 2019s grid.

entries.verdict: THE FLOOR EXISTS AND IT IS LARGE ENOUGH TO MATTER. One flight, two deliveries, zero engine diff: canopy IoU 0.7376 and a 1.3pp citywide canopy-area gap, read from phase4/qc/sameflight_consistency.csv (the row's own note records the conditions). Two consequences, both load-bearing downstream: (1) single-year map steps inside +-1.3pp are processing, not trees — this is the error floor trend8_uniform_rgb's decision rule carries and the reason its interior wobble was declared unreadable; (2) it is the bound overlap_floor's same-window cross-delivery test was judged against, where the 2017 CoE-vs-King pair came in at one-ninth of it, confirming the noise model rather than breaking it. The IoU is the blunter of the two readings: a 0.74 IoU between two products of the SAME photons is the cleanest statement in the repo of how much of a canopy map is the processing chain.

entries.decision_rule: Written before any run exists. SAMPLE: fixed ground blocks, stratified and screened (CHM coverage in both epochs, coreg-quiet, radiometric representativeness), split train/selection/test ONCE; the same blocks for every arm; train and early-stop on train/selection blocks, policy-C threshold chosen on selection blocks, scores read from test blocks only. NOISE FLOOR: the max pairwise |delta| among t1_2011s_base{,_s2,_s3} on the primary statistic; any arm delta at or below it is UNDETERMINED, never a win. PRIMARY STATISTIC: recall at precision 0.75 from the test-block sweep (curve-matched); F1 at the arm's own policy-C point is secondary. KILL RULE (pre-launch, free): a lidar-adder arm whose additions raster changes under 2% of its year's labeled sample pixels is STRUCK before launch and recorded here — it cannot move anything. VERDICTS: lidar-adder pathway CONFIRMED if the adder beats base by more than the floor in >=2 of {2006s, 2011s, 2016}; lidar-input likewise; NIR CONFIRMED only if nir beats base on BOTH 2016 and 2019n (one of two = sensor-specific, reported as such); corruption doses produce a dose-response slope (calibration, no pass/fail). 2020 arms are the sanity anchor: a "win" appearing ONLY on 2020 is suspect (its labels are least wrong; little to correct). GPU: 2xA100 concurrency cap; utilization reported as registry step-hours / session wall-hours with target >=0.85; torch-free steps run on CPU VMs, never on the A100s. Launch flags per arm are generated into this file's arm `extra` lists when the Phase-0 builders land, BEFORE the queue is generated; the science content above does not change after results exist. Launch itself remains Kam's (GPU gate).
entries.headline: Floor (max pairwise |delta| among 2011s base/s2/s3, recall@prec0.75 test blocks) = 0.0085.
entries.hypothesis: The training-side knobs the recipe audit left open — lidar as label context, lidar as an input channel, and the 4th (NIR) band — are testable cheaply on a fixed, screened, spatially-split ground sample before any full-archive spend (design: TIER1_SCIENCE_SAMPLE_PLAN_2026-09-02.md). What would change our mind per question: a lidar-adder win above the measured noise floor in >=2 of the 3 non-2020 years says projected labels are correctably wrong and the 36-run should train on lidar-gated labels; an input-channel win says the model is information-starved, not just label-limited; an NIR win on BOTH sensors says the archive's 4-band years deserve 4-band arms. Null results above the floor close those questions with numbers instead of instinct.

entries.decision_rule: Written before launch. OPERATING-POINT POLICY IS C (Kam, 2026-09-01, after Reports/RECIPE_AUDIT_2026-09-01.md): each arm's deployed threshold is selected by select_indep_threshold.py from its dense independent sweep - criterion f1_plateau_hi_d005 (the HIGHEST k whose F1 sits within 0.005 of the curve's peak, on forest_wetland, raw prob). Rationale measured on the pilot curves BEFORE any 36-run arm exists: both are flat within 0.005 across a 3x threshold range, so strict argmax would deploy the recall-most edge of a plateau the metric cannot distinguish; preferring the precision-most end suits a crown deliverable scored against C-CAP's broad canopy definition. Fallback for an unscorable sweep = fixed 0.5 with a loud flag, NEVER the circular best_f1_thresh. In-queue postproc masks are PLACEHOLDERS (circular threshold); final masks are re-cut post-run at the policy-C threshold on free CPU (postproc --infer-thresh from the registry) and re-scored. An arm PASSES when all six steps verify, qc_indep scores it, and its selection is non-EDGE (or EDGE inspected and accepted). The campaign lands when every arm passes or is listed as a named exception - failures are reported, never hidden. 2006s and 2011s are ADOPTED from hard_year_pilot (identical recipe, tags hy_e3_*) rather than re-run - ~4-6 A100-hr saved; their policy-C re-cut happens with the fleet's. Champion promotion per year remains Kam's call (champion_arms.csv), as does launch (GPU gate: 2xA100 cap, ~65-70 A100-hr estimated for 34 arms, babysitter on every bootstrap).
